fields.outcome: A documentation author can execute a reusable modular browser journey containing navigation, interaction, scrolling, waits, and observable assertions against an authorized web application.
fields.scope: Generalize the declarative journey executor and capture manifest for public and authenticated journeys. Add scroll, wait, select, and assertion actions with stable role/name targets and deterministic diagnostics. Exclude natural-language planning, DOM replay, polished video rendering, and source-code dependency mapping.
fields.acceptance: A representative public-site-style journey executes deterministically, validates expected visible state and URLs, records stable module and step identities, and does not require credentials unless a step references a credential environment variable.
fields.decisions: Keep the journey object as the executable source of truth. Use user-visible role/name locators and explicit postconditions. Treat action timing as declarative input so the same journey can feed video and DOM renderers.
fields.verification: Unit-test every added action with a Playwright-compatible page double, run a real Chromium fixture journey, validate the generated manifest, and retain failure diagnostics for incorrect postconditions.
fields.changes: Implemented schema-shaped JSON execution, credential-optional public journeys, role/name and exact-text targets, select, deterministic timed scroll, bounded waits, visible-state and URL assertions, preservation of publication and dependency metadata, and safe module/step diagnostics.
fields.dependencies: Builds on st-02 capture and manifest behavior. Supplies the executor contract consumed by st-05.
fields.risks: Ambiguous responsive controls and arbitrary waits can create plausible but incorrect tours; assertions and bounded timing are required.

criteria.expectation: The executor supports goto, click, fill, select, scroll, wait, and assert actions used by generic product journeys.
A journey without credential references runs without requiring username or password environment variables.
URL and visible-element assertions fail with the responsible module and step IDs.
Generic action details needed for replay remain schema-valid and stable in generated capture artifacts.
Wait and scroll durations are explicit, finite, and validated before browser execution.
Existing authenticated profile capture behavior remains supported.
